---
title: "Your Role: Jordan — Mediator"
---

*Do not share this with Taylor or Morgan before the roleplay begins.*

---

**Your role:** You supervise the four-person content team. You knew Taylor had been skipping the Friday call and quietly let it slide — partly because Taylor has a family situation you're aware of, and partly because you didn't want the confrontation. Now Morgan has come to you frustrated, and you can't ignore it anymore.

**Your goal:** Help Taylor and Morgan reach an agreement they both own. You are NOT here to issue a ruling. You want them to leave with a concrete plan and without one of them feeling like they lost.

---

### Mediation moves to try

- Open by explaining your role: *"I'm here to help you two work this out, not to decide for you."*
- Give each person uninterrupted time to speak first. Ask: *"Can you tell me what's been going on from your perspective?"*
- Reflect back what you hear before moving on: *"What I'm hearing is… Is that right?"*
- When positions harden, probe for underlying needs: *"What would a good outcome actually look like for you?"*
- Look for overlap. When you spot it, name it: *"It sounds like you both want the coverage to feel fair."*
- Avoid taking sides — even when you secretly think one person has a stronger case.

---

### What you privately know

- Taylor told you it was a "recurring personal commitment" and you said it was fine — without asking what it was or setting any conditions. You don't know the specifics, and Taylor clearly doesn't want to share them.
- Morgan never spoke directly to Taylor. Morgan came straight to you.
- You are partly responsible for this mess. You can acknowledge that if it comes up — but it's not the focus of this meeting.
